chapter: New York, the Kentucky Club and the high-hat
title: Introducing the high-hat to New York drummers
summary: The factory sends the first high-hat to Greer; he demonstrates it in Harlem and takes 30 orders in one night.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: They hadn't invented them. I'm glad you asked me that. We were playing the Kentucky Club, they had two flat boards on the floor, just mashed them together, you know, step on them with that foot. So one day from my factory, the guy come to New York and Kaiser Marshall was playing with Fletcher, up the street at Roseland, so he come with this thing, high-hat, first time it come out and the guy brought it to me first.

He said 'We want you to play this and demonstrate this for us,' so man, 'I can't play that thing,' so he said 'It's easy.' He showed me, 'And your legs won't get tired.' Used to get tired patting that board, on the floor. So I took this damn thing and after a few tries, I begin to experiment with the thing, and I found out, I could do the same thing on the high-hat, that I could do on the snare drum.
So now I'm the only one in New York that got it.

So, everybody used to hang out,/all the clubs up in Harlem, so I take this thing up to Harlem, I say man, I got -- I told Kaiser Marshall, you all are old fashioned, I got the thing, I got the thing. I am still working for my company, you know. I said, you ain't never heard of high hat. What's a high hat. I said I show you, so I take it and I show them.

So the piano player was sitting down, we had a place called the Hooper's Club, next to the Lafayette Theatre, where all the musicians used to hang out. Big place, big bassman, used to gamble, played pool, played cards and buy food -- buy nice food, but everybody -- somebody playing the piano, had a drummer there, so I take that thing down there, and start showing them and they say can we get some. I must have got 30 orders that night.
And the man and the guys -- that's how the high hat come --
Now, the one that you were playing then, was that the short one?
No, this one, about this big. This is it. Just like this.
That little short wooden thing was just two cymbals two boards,/and a spring, you just pat it on the floor, about this high. The high hat is this tall.
Oh, right, so the one you were playing before, it was two pieces of wood with the cymbals on it. And a
Everybody played like that. MR. CROUCH: little spring. / So you get that whoosh --
Just pop, pop -- you couldn't get that like you get on a high hat. That's right.
So you premiered the high hat for the drummers in New York.
That's right. Drummers every-- They bought me one to demonstrate and everybody say how do you get them, so I give them the address in Elkhart, Indiana.
Did you get any kind of commission for orders that you got or did they just give you free drums?
No. Everytime something new come out in the drums, they would send them to me, it didn't cost me nothing.
